why: D4, from both sides. An extension `fun Slug.tidy()` is a **free function under the package module** — `java:shop.text.tidy`, never `java:shop.text.Slug.tidy` — because the receiver type does not own it; attaching it would hang a CONTAINS edge off a type that in real code usually lives in another module or in the SDK. The call side has to agree: `slug.tidy()` looks exactly like a member call and must still resolve to the free function. The plain top-level `shorten(slug)` is here as the contrast — same module-level id, no receiver.

false_positives.why: PREDICTED BEFORE SCORING. `slug.tidy()` is syntactically a member call, so attaching the extension to its receiver type is the one tempting fabrication in Kotlin (D4, risks §11) — it reads naturally and is what a Java-trained reader expects. `Slug` does not declare `tidy`; the package does.
